documents.title: 01_experiment_brief.md
documents.text:
# Cedar pulse local replay brief

All figures in this workspace are invented synthetic local measurements for evaluation. They describe no actual deployment or customer devices.

Experiment: Cedar pulse. Run: CP-31. Input: 400 fabricated sensor events. Window: synthetic clock 10:00:00 through 10:10:00. Workers: Vela-east and Vela-west. The acceptance goal is a p95 event latency at most 150 milliseconds, for the overall run and for each individual worker. Lower latency is better.

Two records cover this exact run and window: the bench notebook and the dashboard export. Both are unreviewed draft records. Neither is designated authoritative, and neither supersedes the other. There is no reconciliation or rerun record in this workspace.

All conclusions must stay within this local synthetic replay. There is no documented relationship to production service quality.

documents.title: 02_bench_notebook.md
documents.text:
# Cedar pulse bench notebook

Invented synthetic local measurement. Record state: unreviewed draft.

Run CP-31; synthetic clock window 10:00:00 through 10:10:00; 400 fabricated sensor events. Overall p95 event latency: 162 milliseconds.

Worker Vela-east: p95 event latency 138 milliseconds; peak resident memory 1.8 GiB.
Worker Vela-west: p95 event latency 171 milliseconds; peak resident memory 2.3 GiB.

Mean electrical power for Vela-east: not measured. Mean electrical power for Vela-west: not measured. No wall power meter was connected during CP-31. No energy reading is available for either worker.

# Cedar pulse local worker inventory

Synthetic invented inventory for a local evaluation fixture.

Vela-east: power adapter nameplate rating 65 watts.
Vela-west: power adapter nameplate rating 95 watts.

These are adapter ratings, not measured average operating power. Neither rating is a measurement of energy consumed during CP-31. No conclusion about comparative energy efficiency follows from the nameplate ratings alone.
